decision: routed the task to figure-it-out with exploratory prototypes under it
why: the ask spans a React-free component, a refresh redesign and DOM patching from mutation events, so no single playbook fits and the design space needs competing prototypes

decision: found @sanity/visual-editing/enable-visual-editing (standalone) and @sanity/visual-editing/optimistic (actor, listeners) as the public seams for a React-free client
why: the standalone entry still renders overlays with React internally, but consumers never import React or @astrojs/react; the optimistic entry exposes the dataset mutator actor fed by presentation/snapshot-event
result: no pnpm patch needed for the first pass

decision: chose ppsg7ml5/cody-e2e (public, empty) as the live sandbox dataset
why: SANITY_TEST_STUDIO_AUTH_TOKEN is an editor token for ppsg7ml5 and cody-e2e holds only system docs, so writes are isolated and reversible; public dataset lets the frontend read published content token-free
evidence: api.sanity.io/v2021-06-07/projects response; groq count(*)=38 system docs

decision: verified enableVisualEditing() boots from a plain <script> in the React-free minimal app
why: riskiest unknown first: Vite bundles React transitively for @sanity/visual-editing, the app itself needs no @astrojs/react and renders zero astro-island elements
evidence: /tmp/live-preview-lab/probe.mjs output: overlayHost true, reactIslands 0, no @astrojs/react in apps/minimal/package.json

decision: chose idiomorph (0BSD, 3.4 kB gzip) for the in-place refresh instead of body replace or Astro swapFunctions
why: keeps node identity so focus, scroll and stega text nodes survive; swapFunctions needs astro:transitions/client which only exists on Astro >= 4.15 while we support 2 through 7
result: open until measured against body replace

decision: instant text patches read the dataset mutator actor exported by @sanity/visual-editing/optimistic instead of registering loader queries
why: the actor already receives every mutation for documents on the page via presentation/snapshot-event; loader/query-listen would need the server to emit each page query and gives the same string values for stega nodes

decision: stega perspective param picks the exact document variant (published, drafts, versions) a text node came from
why: createEditUrl sets perspective=published for published sources and omits it for drafts, so the patcher never shows draft text on a published-perspective page

decision: kept the React VisualEditingComponent export as a deprecated wrapper over the same runtime
why: it is public API documented for custom refresh functions; removing it is a semver-major call for the maintainers

decision: morph keeps client-injected DOM: overlay host, dev toolbar, Vite error overlay, head styles and scripts, elements with data-astro-transition-persist
why: server HTML never contains client-injected nodes, so a naive morph would strip cookie banners, chat widgets and dev styles on every refresh

decision: built a Presentation stand-in (comlink controller + real Content Lake listener) instead of booting a Studio
why: deterministic, token-light, and it exercises the exact protocol; the one surprise was that @sanity/visual-editing answers in the legacy sanity/channels format, so the controller needs createCompatibilityActors like the real Presentation tool

decision: captured the reload baseline: content back at ~140 ms but Presentation reconnect takes 0.7 to 3.7 s and scroll needs restoring
why: the old default was window.location.reload(); this is the old value the morph is compared against

decision: morph refresh: ~125 ms, no navigation, scroll 300 to 300, channel stays connected, 0 console errors
why: same page, same harness, manual refresh from Presentation

decision: text patches only rewrite a node when its text is a value the document held before (bounded snapshot history)
why: the first version cached decoded sources per text node and rewrote Spirited Away over The Iron Giant after a morph reordered the list; the rule also protects transformed text from being overwritten with raw values
evidence: run-morph-1.json titles vs years mismatch; src/visual-editing/live-text.ts outdatedValue

decision: listener-to-query lag measured at 107-395 ms with one earlier outlier over 660 ms
why: a morph fetched right after the mutation event returned HTML older than the event and reverted the instant text patch
result: drives the 500 ms delay, stale retry and 1 s settle pass

decision: instant stega text patch lands at event arrival (169-254 ms after commit), derived values via morph at ~1.0 s typical and 2.0 s worst case
why: four consecutive runs, same harness, DOM order and years verified after each

decision: unit suite green at 118 tests with 93.7 percent line coverage; check:package green after adding .js extensions to shipped relative imports
why: attw node16 ESM failed on extensionless imports in the copied .ts sources, the same convention the old React component used

decision: demo timing corrected: the first recording measured DOM latency from the sync commit round trip, not from the write
why: the page had patched the text 4 ms after the mutation event all along; the driver only started polling after commit() resolved

decision: checked @sanity/visual-editing-standalone 2.0.1 as a replacement for @sanity/visual-editing
why: it would drop react, react-dom, styled-components and @sanity/ui from a no-Studio consumer's lockfile, which is the remaining React footprint after this PR
evidence: npm registry metadata; /tmp/ve-standalone/package/dist/index.d.ts exports only createDataAttribute and enableVisualEditing
result: works for overlays, blocks on one missing export

decision: swapped the import in the built copy and measured both packages on the same harness scenario
why: the exports list said the optimistic actor is absent, and the measurement puts a number on what that costs
evidence: /tmp/live-preview-lab/scenario-standalone.mjs; standalone title at 1789 ms vs 251-278 ms today, both with manual refresh at ~140 ms and no navigation

decision: kept @sanity/visual-editing on this PR and removed the experimental standalone dependency
why: standalone omits the optimistic entry that drives instant text, and importing it unconditionally would ship a second React to every embedded-Studio user, whose Studio already peers on react
evidence: packages/sanity-astro/package.json unchanged for dependencies; @sanity/visual-editing-csm and mutator code present but unexported in the standalone bundle

decision: measured production bundles both ways: 258,618 vs 259,571 bytes gzip, so standalone buys no wire-size win
why: the install-ergonomics case is real but the bundle case is not, which changes how the tradeoff should be presented
result: no wire win, graph win only

decision: two of three adversarial reviewers independently found the held-before rule unsound and the React wrapper only half-delegating
why: agreement across model families is the high-signal case, so both went straight to act-on without waiting for the third

decision: replaced document-snapshot history with per-field verbatim calibration plus 64 raw values
why: equality with an earlier raw value is not provenance; an upper-cased rendering that once matched would be overwritten and then re-overwritten by the post-morph repair
evidence: src/visual-editing/live-text.ts outdatedValue and observe; three new tests

decision: re-measured end to end after the review fixes: manual 125-128 ms, title 196-230 ms, reorder 997-1290 ms, zero errors
why: the fixes touched the hot path, so the numbers had to be re-earned rather than assumed

decision: noted without action: version-perspective nodes never patch because upstream observes only draft and published ids
why: it is a graceful no-op rather than corruption, and fixing it needs a change in DocumentReporter, not here
evidence: GPT reviewer finding 1; @sanity/visual-editing dist/VisualEditing-*.js DocumentReporter observe calls

decision: dismissed: returning false from refresh when live-text already scheduled a morph
why: false suppresses the refreshing and refreshed round trip that drives the Studio's loading indicator; dropping the extra settle pass fixed the duplication without hiding state

decision: noted: the bootstrap script ships even when enabled is false
why: Astro hoists component scripts, so this is inherent; the guard makes it a no-op that loads no further chunk, about 1.5 kB

decision: full suite green after the review round: 133 tests, 96.0 percent lines on visual-editing, check:package exit 0
why: the review fixes touched every module in the runtime, so the gates were re-run rather than assumed
